title: New Grand Rapids boutique offers space to 'be enchanted by beauty' - NewsBreak
text:
By Katie Rosendale ,
10 hours ago GRAND RAPIDS, Mich. (WOOD) — A new boutique in Grand Rapids’ East Hills neighborhood has a lofty goal: to delight and enchant those who walk through its door.
Wisteria and Sunshine is located at 949 Cherry St. SE near Lake Drive SE. The store is full of greenery and drenched in color, with chandeliers and 14-foot ceilings.
Catfish, po’boys, beignets and more: Sugah Please celebrates six months in Grand Rapids “I just really want this place to be a space where people can enjoy in the delight of shopping, but also just be enchanted by beauty, whether it’s the beauty of plants or the beauty of goods that are imported from all over,” owner Naomi Stout told News 8. “Even if you’re not buying and you’re just walking around and you just need a little reprieve, I just want people to remember that shopping in person is a lovely experience. It’s a delight.”
Wisteria and Sunshine in Grand Rapids. (July 29, 2026) Wisteria and Sunshine in Grand Rapids. (July 29, 2026) Wisteria and Sunshine in Grand Rapids. (July 29, 2026) Wisteria and Sunshine in Grand Rapids. (July 29, 2026) On the shelves, you’ll find artfully arranged displays of candles, jewelry, greeting cards, porcelain dishes, recipe books, home decor, clothing and more. Stout highlighted the selection of handbags from Italy and the “tulipieres,” a special type of vase from the Netherlands. The store will also function as an art gallery, with local and fine art for sale.
“The store is for everybody,” Stout explained. “I know that women tend to shop generally more than men, but I want the store to be for anyone that just needs a reprieve from their day, someone who just wants to be inspired, someone who might have a broken heart and just needs a space that feels peaceful and beautiful to walk through.”
As icon marks milestone, Wealthy Street keeps growing Wisteria and Sunshine in Grand Rapids. (July 29, 2026) The boutique’s name, Wisteria and Sunshine, is drawn from the 1991 film “Enchanted April.”
“That movie really moved me. It was about some women who are not at the best place in their lives, and they rent a villa in Italy and become their best selves,” Stout said. “The beauty of the Italian environment really transforms them and allows them to become who they’re meant to be.”
In the movie, she explained, “there’s an ad in the paper for ‘those who appreciate wisteria and sunshine.’ That’s where I got the name from, and I just really felt it in my soul.”
Rotating menu, seasonal dishes: Watusi opening soon in Grand Rapids Stout herself has a “really diverse” career background, which includes eight years managing a retail gift store in Grand Rapids. This is her first time owning a shop.
“I have been wanting to own my own store for years,” she said. “Managing a retail store in the past really made me understand that I was capable of doing that. And I had a vision for my own taste and what I wanted it to feel and look like.”
She spent months looking for a building, then found the space on Cherry Street.
“I feel so lucky to be here. It is just such a gracious space with so much history. It’s lovely,” Stout said. “And I also think that Cherry Street is a really wonderful place to be. There’s wonderful shops — Commune, Covet, Le Bon (Macaron) — all the places around here, we complement each other really well.”
Inside WOODTV.com: Building West Michigan Wisteria and Sunshine in Grand Rapids. (July 29, 2026) Stout moved into the building in June and held a soft opening earlier this month. On Saturday, she will host a grand opening celebration starting at 10 a.m. It’s free to attend and the first 50 people through the door will get goodie bags.
“There’s various things in the store that I love that will be in the bags, as well as a macaron from next door,” the owner said.
Each bag will also include a coupon for 20% off any item and a raffle ticket. Throughout the day, Stout will be pulling numbers and giving away items from the store. Then from 4 p.m. to 6 p.m., attendees can enjoy snacks and live entertainment from a jazz band.
Wisteria and Sunshine is open 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. Tuesday through Saturday and 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. Sunday.
